intro: Office supervisors already lead people, plan work and solve problems, so management is the natural next step. The closest of the 25 careers below is Administrative Services Managers, with a 92% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $114,130, which is 64% more than the $69,500 office supervisors earn.
why_it_works: Running an office team means assigning work, coaching staff and keeping service steady when people are out. O*NET rates coordination and social perceptiveness at 4 out of 5 for this job. Administrative, operations and HR management use the same leadership skills. Many of those roles ask for a bachelor's degree. The gaps are budgets, technology design and managing materials.
tips: Volunteer for budget planning in your department; financial management is your main gap.
Project Management Specialists earn $102,320, which is 47% more, and a project certificate can help.
HR Managers earn $149,280 if you enjoy hiring and coaching, though most need a degree.

faq.q: What jobs can former office supervisors do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Administrative Services Managers (92%), non-retail sales supervisors (89%) and Gambling Managers (82%), based on O*NET 31.0. General and Operations Managers are also 82% matched and earn $105,770, which is 52% more than office supervisors earn.

faq.q: Which careers for office supervisors pay more?
faq.a: 18 of the 25 matches pay more than $69,500. Financial Managers earn $166,570 (140% more), Human Resources Managers $149,280 (115% more) and Compensation and Benefits Managers $149,230 (115% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. All three usually need a bachelor's degree.

faq.q: Do office supervisors need a degree to move up?
faq.a: Often. Only 11 of the 25 matches need no more education than office supervisors already have, and 5 of the top 10. A bachelor's degree is common in close matches, held by 45% of workers, so many supervisors finish one part-time.

faq.q: What skills should office supervisors build?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are managing financial resources, operation and control, technology design and managing materials. Managing people already rates 3.75 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so budgets and systems are the main steps toward manager roles.
